extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Plato; readers of political philosophy and classical theory of education/government
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for educating, selecting, housing, and regulating the guardian (ruling/warrior) class in an ideal city — covering music, gymnastic, diet, medical practice, tests of character, property rules, and myths to sustain loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: True love as temperate love of beauty and order
rubrics_metrics.description: “True love is a love of beauty and order—temperate and harmonious.” Mad or intemperate pleasure has no affinity to virtue and must be excluded from the lovers and beloved of the right sort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleasure that deprives a man of the use of his faculties is akin to madness and wantonness; rules of intimacy should be limited (e.g., 'no other familiarity to his love than a father would use to his son'), and excesses are to be deemed coarseness and bad taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical education: simplicity to foster temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity in music is 'the parent of temperance in the soul.' Complex, panharmonic music engenders licence; soft, melancholy airs can 'melt and waste' the spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach simple, restrained melodies that cultivate order and self-control. Avoid 'melody and song composed in the panharmonic style' and prolonged softening music which leads to effeminacy, irritability, or moral weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gymnastic education: simple, military conditioning for endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Gymnastic (physical training) should begin early, be careful, continue through life, and for warrior-athletes be 'a finer sort of training' producing wakefulness, keenness, and endurance rather than the sleepy, illness-prone bodies of ordinary athletes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise military-style, robust training and simple regimen (soldiers' fare, roast meats) over athletic regimes that build bulk but impair responsiveness. Avoid overemphasis on muscle-development alone, which produces ferocity and ignorance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize music and gymnastic to produce balanced souls
rubrics_metrics.description: The two principles in human nature—the spirited and the philosophical—require arts answering to them (music and gymnastic) so that these 'two principles... may be relaxed or drawn tighter until they are duly harmonized.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine music and gymnastic 'in the fairest proportions' so guardians are both gentle and spirited: temperate and courageous. Anti-patterns: musician-only (softness/effeminacy) or athlete-only (brutal ferocity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstinence from intoxication for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians 'must abstain from intoxication'; a guardian should be the last to get drunk and to be unable to know where he is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make intoxication unacceptable for guardians; it is absurd that a guardian should require another guardian to look after him. This rule protects competence and vigilance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, robust diet appropriate to soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Diet for guardian/warriors should be simple and suited to campaigning: e.g., roast meats requiring minimal preparation; no sweet sauces, refined Sicilian cookery, Corinthian girls as temptations, or Athenian confectionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid culinary refinements and delicacies which lead to disease and softness. Use Homeric soldiers' fare as model: food convenient for soldiers, promoting health and endurance rather than luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical practice aligned with the state's interest; avoid cultivating illness
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicine should not 'educate diseases' by encouraging valetudinarian habits; physicians should treat definite ailments and not lengthen 'good-for-nothing' lives which are of no use to the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit medical intervention for genuine, recoverable conditions (wounds, epidemics), but avoid therapies aimed at prolonging unproductive lives or fostering chronic hypochondria. Critique of Herodicus: torturing oneself with lingering treatments is undesirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician qualifications: knowledge plus experience of disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The most skilful physicians are those who have combined knowledge of their art with the greatest experience of disease; they may be personally less robust, having had many illnesses themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer physicians acquainted intimately with varied constitutions and ailments, since they 'cure the body with the mind' and require experiential familiarity with sickness to diagnose and treat effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge qualifications: learned knowledge of evil by observation, not personal vice
rubrics_metrics.description: A good judge 'ought not therefore to have been trained among vicious minds' or have committed crimes himself; he should learn of evil by late and long observation of others, not from personal contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select judges who are mature, experienced observers of human wrongdoing (older rather than young), guided by knowledge and virtue rather than cynical personal practice of vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select guardians by demonstrated love for the city and resistance to corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose among the guardians those who 'in their whole life show the greatest eagerness to do what is for the good of their country, and the greatest repugnance to do what is against her interests.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor subjects at every age for preservation of resolution, love of the city's interests, and aversion to self-serving conduct. The right men show consistent character across life stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous multi-stage testing (temptation, force, enchantment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be 'watched at every age' and tried by tests of theft (argument), force (pain/grief), and enchantment (pleasure/fear); also trials in toils, pains, pleasures and terrors—'proved more thoroughly than gold is proved in the furnace.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement staged trials: exposure to deceptive argument, simulated terrors and pleasures, noisy tumult (like taking colts) to reveal timidity or nobility, and repeated tests across youth and maturity. Appoint only those who emerge 'victorious and pure.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal living and strict property restrictions for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians 'should have no property of his own beyond what is absolutely necessary; neither should they have a private house... provisions should be only such as are required by trained warriors... they should agree to receive from the citizens a fixed rate of pay... and they will go to mess and live together like soldiers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit guardians from owning gold or silver or residing under the same roof with such wealth (may not touch, wear, or drink from gold/silver). These measures prevent accumulation of private interests that corrupt guardians into tyrants or enemies of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design dwellings and habits to avoid tempting guardians to tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians' dwellings must 'shield them against the cold of winter and the heat of summer' but be 'houses of soldiers, and not of shop-keepers'—arranged so as neither to impair virtue nor tempt them to prey on other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide functional, communal housing and a lifestyle oriented toward duty rather than private comfort or luxury to reduce risks of abuse of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a civic myth ('royal lie') and role-assignment with controlled mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell citizens a convenient falsehood (the old Phoenician tale) that people are born from the earth with different metals (gold, silver, brass/iron) marking rulers, auxiliaries, and craftsmen; yet allow for transposition if nature indicates (a golden child of artisans may be raised to guardianship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the myth to foster mutual loyalty and identification with the city. While proclaiming 'purity of the race' rhetoric for cohesion, institute tests of nature (not pity) to raise or lower children between classes when their constitution warrants it. Recognise this will take generations to implant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise the good of the whole State over the private happiness of any class
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in founding the State is 'not the disproportionate happiness of any one class, but the greatest happiness of the whole'; guardians' dispensations (e.g., lack of private wealth) are justified by the fitness of role within the harmonious whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies by their contribution to overall justice and order rather than by whether one class appears materially advantaged; avoid making any class 'happy' in a way that undermines its function or the unity of the State.
